ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in the right-angled $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $AC=8$, $BC=6$. The point $M$ starts from point $C$ and moves along the segment $CA$ towards point $A$, connecting $BM$, and $MN \perp BM$ intersects side $AB$ at point $N$. If $CM=2$, what is the length of segment $AN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $NH \perp AC$ at point $H$ through point $N$, \\
$\because \angle C=90^\circ$, $AC=8$, $BC=6$, \\
$\therefore AB=\sqrt{AC^2+BC^2}=10$, \\
$\because \sin A=\frac{NH}{AN}=\frac{BC}{AB}=\frac{3}{5}$, $\tan A=\frac{NH}{AH}=\frac{BC}{AC}=\frac{3}{4}$, \\
$\therefore AN=\frac{5}{3}NH$, $AH=\frac{4}{3}NH$, \\
$\because \angle C=\angle BMN=\angle MNH=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle BMC+\angle NMH=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle CBM=90^\circ-\angle BMC=\angle NMH$, \\
$\therefore \tan\angle CBM=\frac{CM}{BC}=\tan\angle NHM=\frac{NH}{MH}$, \\
thus, $\frac{2}{6}=\frac{NH}{8-2-\frac{4}{3}NH}$, \\
Solving gives: $NH=\frac{18}{13}$, \\
$\therefore AN=\frac{5}{3}NH=\frac{5}{3} \times \frac{18}{13}=\boxed{\frac{30}{13}}$.

solver_metadata.cot_raw: 图像描述：图中是直角三角形ABC，C在左下，B在C的正上方，A在右下方，因此AB是斜边。点M位于底边CA上，点N位于斜边AB上，图中连接了BM和MN；题干给出MN垂直于BM。推理：按指定向量法建立坐标系，取C=(0,0)，A=(8,0)，B=(0,6)。因为CM=2且M在CA上，所以M=(2,0)。AB=\sqrt{8^2+6^2}=10，从A到B的单位向量为((-8,6)/10)=(-4/5,3/5)。设AN=s，则N=A+s(-4/5,3/5)=(8-4s/5,3s/5)。于是N-M=(6-4s/5,3s/5)，B-M=(-2,6)。由MN\perp BM，得(N-M)\cdot(B-M)=0，即-2(6-4s/5)+6(3s/5)=0。化简为-12+26s/5=0，所以s=30/13。因此AN=30/13。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, in the right-angled $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $AC=8$, $BC=6$. The point $M$ starts from point $C$ and moves along the segment $CA$ towards point $A$, connecting $BM$, and $MN \perp BM$ intersects side $AB$ at point $N$. If $CM=2$, what is the length of segment $AN$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $NH \perp AC$ at point $H$ through point $N$, \\
$\because \angle C=90^\circ$, $AC=8$, $BC=6$, \\
$\therefore AB=\sqrt{AC^2+BC^2}=10$, \\
$\because \sin A=\frac{NH}{AN}=\frac{BC}{AB}=\frac{3}{5}$, $\tan A=\frac{NH}{AH}=\frac{BC}{AC}=\frac{3}{4}$, \\
$\therefore AN=\frac{5}{3}NH$, $AH=\frac{4}{3}NH$, \\
$\because \angle C=\angle BMN=\angle MNH=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle BMC+\angle NMH=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle CBM=90^\circ-\angle BMC=\angle NMH$, \\
$\therefore \tan\angle CBM=\frac{CM}{BC}=\tan\angle NHM=\frac{NH}{MH}$, \\
thus, $\frac{2}{6}=\frac{NH}{8-2-\frac{4}{3}NH}$, \\
Solving gives: $NH=\frac{18}{13}$, \\
$\therefore AN=\frac{5}{3}NH=\frac{5}{3} \times \frac{18}{13}=\boxed{\frac{30}{13}}$
raw_record.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is right triangle ABC, C is at the lower left and is the right-angle vertex, CB goes vertically upward to B, CA goes horizontally rightward to A; M is located on CA near C, B and M are connected; N is located on the hypotenuse AB, and the line segment MN connected from M to N intersects BM forming a perpendicular relationship. Then reason: According to the specified coordinate method, take C=(0,0), A=(8,0), B=(0,6). Because CM=2 and M is on CA, M=(2,0). The slope of line BM is (0-6)/(2-0)=-3, therefore the slope of MN perpendicular to BM is 1/3, and the equation through M is y=(x-2)/3. The hypotenuse AB passes through A=(8,0), B=(0,6), and its slope is (0-6)/(8-0)=-3/4, so the equation of AB is y=6-(3/4)x. Find the intersection point N: set (x-2)/3=6-(3/4)x, multiply by 12 to get 4x-8=72-9x, so 13x=80, x=80/13; substituting gives y=(80/13-2)/3=18/13. Therefore N=(80/13,18/13). Thus AN=sqrt((8-80/13)^2+(0-18/13)^2)=sqrt((24/13)^2+(18/13)^2)=sqrt(900/169)=30/13.
